subject: Re: Order Form Exhibit — delivery buckets, cap/floor mechanics and redline
messages:
From: Emma Holt <emma.holt@orbittech.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-08T09:12:00Z
Subject: Exhibit B redline + questions on delivery buckets and pricing floor

Karthik / Laura / Ben,

Thanks for sending the draft order form last week. Attached is OrbitTech's annotated Exhibit B (PDF) with our proposed edits. A few high-level items we need clarity on before legal will sign: 

- Delivery buckets: your Exhibit B separates 'Reserved' vs 'Burst' buckets but doesn't define the true-up cadence when usage moves between buckets (monthly vs quarterly). We need contract language that ties true-up to invoices.
- Pricing floor / cap mechanics: Section 2.3 implies a dynamic cap that steps quarterly — our finance team insists on a fixed annual floor to avoid mid-year spikes.
- Packaging discounts: the 10% SKU bundle discount appears to apply per-invoice; we want it to be applied at the customer account level for the billing period (so credits can carry forward).

We've flagged exact lines in the attached PDF. Can you confirm Redwood's willingness to: (1) specify month-end true-up tied to invoice cycle, (2) convert the cap schedule to an annual max with quarterly adjustments only by mutual written amendment, and (3) clarify discount application scope?

We'd like to get this wrapped before OrbitTech's procurement board meets on 2026-11-16.

Thanks,

Emma Holt
Head of Procurement | OrbitTech, Inc.
emma.holt@orbittech.com | +1 (415) 555-0191

Attachment: OrbitTech_Redline_ExhibitB.pdf (annotated PDF, 8 pages)
From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Emma Holt <emma.holt@orbittech.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-08T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Exhibit B redline + questions on delivery buckets and pricing floor

Emma —

Appreciate the annotated PDF and the clear summary. We're aligned on getting this closed before your board date. Quick replies to your three asks below — I'll loop Legal for contract language and Finance for economics confirmation: 

1) True-up cadence: Redwood's standard is monthly invoice-aligned true-ups, but Exhibit B can be explicit. Laura, suggest language to tie bucket movement to 'end-of-month invoice reconciliation' and specify rounding rules.

2) Cap/floor mechanics: We can offer an annual 'hard cap' on billable tokens for the year with quarterly reporting and a documented 'adjustment window' if both parties agree in writing. Ben, can you confirm if finance can accept an annual hard cap with quarterly visibility (no unilateral mid-year reprice)?

3) Discount scope: We typically apply bundle discounts per-billing-account but can agree to account-level application for the period if OrbitTech provides a single billing account ID. Ben, please confirm mechanics for carry-forward credit.

I'll prepare a Redwood counter-redline for Exhibit B with suggested language for the three items and attach it later today. Can we do a short 30-minute call this afternoon (3pm PT) to go over the counter and any sticky points?

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-0142

Attachment: (to follow)
From: laura.bennett@redwood.com <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, emma.holt@orbittech.com
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-08T13:20:00Z
Subject: RE: Exhibit B redline + questions on delivery buckets and pricing floor

Emma / Karthik —

Thanks for the clear flags. I've drafted suggested contract language and a clean counter-redline (attached .docx) that aims to: 

- Define 'Reserved' and 'Burst' buckets (Section 1.1) and set the true-up to 'monthly, final as of the invoice date' with a 30-day dispute window. This keeps reconciliation tied to billing while giving OrbitTech short-term recourse for errors.

- Add an 'Annual Billing Cap' (Section 2.3(a)) that sets the maximum billable units for the 12-month term. Quarterly reports will be provided as visibility only; any change to the cap requires mutual written amendment and a 60-day notice before effect.

- Clarify discount application (Section 3.2): discounts apply at the billing-account level for the invoice period; unused discount value may be carried forward for up to two subsequent invoice periods as a credit, subject to a $0.00 minimum (i.e., no cash refunds).

I also included a small stabilization clause allowing a one-time temporary surcharge waiver during the first 90 days if usage volatility exceeds 300% of forecast, to avoid accidental large overages during the ramp. Please see tracked changes in the attached 'Redwood_Counter_ExhibitB_redline.docx'.

Attachment: Redwood_Counter_ExhibitB_redline.docx (tracked changes)

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Exhibit B redline + questions on delivery buckets and pricing floor

Karthik / Laura —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the counter-redline. We've reviewed Laura's language with our finance/legal teams and have three follow-up items: 

A) Monthly true-up + 30-day dispute window is acceptable; please add an explicit example of rounding behavior (tokens rounded down to nearest 100).

B) Annual Billing Cap: OrbitTech can accept an annual hard cap but asks for a carveout — if Redwood unilaterally applies a 'surcharge' in the first 90 days under the stabilization clause, that amount must not count toward the annual cap. In short: waivers shouldn't erode our cap.

C) Carry-forward credits: two-period carry-forward is fine, but we need a reporting itemization on the invoice showing 'discount applied' and 'credit carried forward' lines for transparency.

Procurement's target is to complete legal review by EOD 2026-11-12. If we can agree on the three bullets above today, I can route the counter to approvals.

Emma Holt
Head of Procurement | OrbitTech, Inc.

Emma —

All good points. Short answers and next steps: 

A) Rounding: Laura will add a one-sentence example to the Exhibit that tokens are rounded to the nearest 100 for billing, with a specific sample calculation included in Annex A.

B) Stabilization carveout: We can add explicit language that surcharge waivers granted by Redwood during the first 90 days are treated as non-billable and do not count against the Annual Billing Cap. Laura, will incorporate.

C) Invoice transparency: Ben will add the invoice line itemization to our billing export and sample invoice, and we'll include a sample in Annex B.

Next steps: Laura will produce a 'clean' Exhibit B with the three clarifications included (rounding example, non-counting waiver language, sample invoice format). I'll schedule a 30-minute alignment call for 3pm PT today to walk through the final redline and, if acceptable, I'll request a DocuSign send later this afternoon.

Action items (owners):
- Laura: finalize clean Exhibit B + Annex A/B (by 3pm PT)
- Ben: confirm invoice line itemization and provide sample invoice PDF (by 2pm PT)
- Emma: confirm procurement board window (EOD 11/12) and confirm you can approve after legal clears (by 12pm PT)

Thanks — talk shortly.

Karthik Iyer
